metadata.title: Left translates of a square integrable function on the Heisenberg group

extraction_notes.note: This arXiv version states the main results of Sections 3-6 without any proofs; the only proof environment is that of Proposition 2.2. The theorems are left without rigor flags since the paper presents them as proved.
The Examples environment holds only its intro sentence; the six numbered examples follow in an itemize outside it. Kept the environment node at its span and emitted each item as a prose example.
Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 2.3 are stated as tools for the omitted proofs and are used by no stated argument, so they remain orphans.

nodes.name: Shift-invariant space
nodes.statement: A closed subspace $V\subset L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ is called shift-invariant if $f\in V\Longrightarrow \tau_{k}f\in V$ for any $k\in \mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Heisenberg group
nodes.statement: The Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$ is a nilpotent Lie group whose underlying manifold is $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}$, where the group operation is defined by $(x,y,t)(x^{\prime},y^{\prime},t^{\prime})=(x+x^{\prime},y+y^{\prime},t+t^{\prime}+\dfrac{1}{2}(x^{\prime}.y-y^{\prime}.x))$ and the Haar measure is the Lebesgue measure  $\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}y\mathrm{d}t$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{H}^n=\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ with the twisted group law and Lebesgue Haar measure.

nodes.name: Standard lattice is a discrete subgroup
nodes.statement: Now it is clear that $\{(2k,l,m):k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n},m\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ is a discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{H}^{n}$.

nodes.name: Stone-von Neumann theorem
conclusions: every infinite dimensional irreducible unitary representation on the Heisenberg group is unitarily equivalent to the representation $\pi_{\lambda}, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}^{\star}$
nodes.statement_short: Every infinite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation of $\mathbb{H}^n$ is equivalent to a Schrodinger representation $\pi_\lambda$.

nodes.name: Group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group
nodes.statement: The group Fourier transform on $\mathbb{H}^n$ is defined to be $$\widehat{f}(\lambda)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{H}^n}f(x,y,t)\pi_\lambda(x,y,t)dxdydt$$ for $f\in L^{1}(\mathbb{H}^n)$. More explicitly, $\widehat{f}(\lambda)$ is the bounded operator acting on $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ (i.e., $\widehat{f}(\lambda)\in \mathcal{B}(L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n}))$) given by $\widehat{f}(\lambda)\varphi=\displaystyle\int\limits_{\mathbb{H}^n}f(x,y,t)\pi_\lambda(x,y,t)\varphi dxdy dt$, where the integral is a Bochner integral taking values in the Hilbert space $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ .
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat f(\lambda)=\int f\,\pi_\lambda$, an operator-valued (Bochner) integral on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$.

nodes.name: Partial inverse Fourier transform in t
nodes.statement: Define $f^\lambda(x,y)=\displaystyle\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}}f(x,y,t)e^{2\pi i\lambda t}dt$ to be the inverse Fourier transform of $f$ in the $t$-variable.

nodes.name: Group Fourier transform via f^lambda
nodes.statement: Thus $\widehat{f}(\lambda)=\displaystyle\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}f^\lambda(x,y)\pi_\lambda(x,y,0)dxdy$.

nodes.name: Operator W_lambda
nodes.statement:
One can write $\widehat{f}(\lambda)=W_\lambda(f^\lambda)$, where $W_{\lambda}(f)$ is given by
$$W_\lambda(f)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}f(x,y)\pi_\lambda(x,y,0)dxdy,$$
for $f\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$.

nodes.name: Convolution on the Heisenberg group
Twisted convolution
Twisted convolution as Heisenberg convolution
nodes.statement: If we define $f^{\#}(z,t)=e^{-2\pi it}f(z)$, then one can show that $f^{\#}* g^{\#}=(f\times g)^{\#}$.

nodes.name: Group Fourier transform of a convolution
nodes.statement: Further, for $f,g\in L^{1}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$, one has $\widehat{f*g}(\lambda)=\widehat{f}(\lambda)\widehat{g}(\lambda),~\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{\star} $, as in the case of Euclidean Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Weyl transform
nodes.statement:
This leads to $W(f\times g)= W(f) W(g)$, where 
$$W(f)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}f(x,y)\pi(x,y)dxdy,$$ called the Weyl transform of $f\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$, by taking $\lambda=1$ in $W_{\lambda}(f)$ and by writing $\pi (x,y)=\pi_{1}(x,y,0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Weyl transform $W(f)=\int f(x,y)\pi(x,y)\,dxdy$ (the case $\lambda=1$ of $W_\lambda$); it turns twisted convolution into composition.

nodes.name: Lattice L in the Heisenberg group
nodes.statement: Let $\mathscr{L}$ be a discrete subgroup of the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^{n}$ such that $\mathbb{H}^{n}/\mathscr{L}$ is compact.

nodes.name: Lattice
nodes.statement: In other words, $\mathscr{L}$ is a lattice in $\mathbb{H}^{n}$.

nodes.name: Principal shift-invariant space V(phi)
nodes.statement:
For $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$, the principal shift-invariant space, $V(\varphi)$, is defined to be  $\overline{span}\{{L_{l}\varphi:l\in\mathscr{L}}\}$, where
$L_{l}\varphi(X)=\varphi(l^{-1}.X),~X\in\mathbb{H}^{n}$.

nodes.name: V(phi) for the standard lattice
nodes.statement: Hence for $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n}),~V(\varphi)$ is taken to be the closed linear span of the collection $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}, m\in\mathbb{Z}\}$.

nodes.name: Twisted translation
nodes.statement:
For $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n}), (k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$, we define the twisted translation of $\varphi$, denoted by $T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi$, as
$$T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi (x,y)= e^{\pi i(x.l-y.k)}\varphi (x-k,y-l),~(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}.$$

nodes.name: Twisted shift-invariant space
nodes.statement: Using this definition, the twisted shift-invariant space of $\varphi$, denoted by $V^{t}(\varphi)$, is  defined to be the closed linear span of $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi: (k,l)\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}\}$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$.

conclusions: which maps $L^{1}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ into the space of bounded operators on  $L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{n})$

conclusions: This map $W$ can be uniquely extended to a bijection from the class of tempered distributions $S^{\prime}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ onto the space of continuous linear maps from $S(\mathbb {R}^{n})$ into  $S^{\prime}(\mathbb {R}^{n})$

nodes.name: Weyl transform of L^2 functions is Hilbert-Schmidt
nodes.statement: If $f\in L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$, then $W(f)\in\mathcal{B}_{2}(L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{n}))$, the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$.

nodes.name: Plancherel formula for the Weyl transform
nodes.statement: \langle W(f), W(g)\rangle_{\mathcal{B}_{2}}=\langle f,g\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})}=\langle K_{f},K_{g}\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})}.
nodes.label: 3peq21

nodes.name: Plancherel theorem for the group Fourier transform
nodes.statement: The group Fourier transform is an isometric isomorphism of $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ onto $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{\star},\mathcal{B}_{2};\\d\mu)$ , where $\mathcal{B}_{2}$ denotes the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ and $d\mu(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{n}d\lambda$.
conclusions: The group Fourier transform is an isometric isomorphism of $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ onto $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{\star},\mathcal{B}_{2};\\d\mu)$

nodes.name: l^2-linear dependence and independence
nodes.statement:
A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is said to be $\ell^{2}$-linearly dependent if there exists a non-zero sequence $\{c_{k}\}\in\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{k}f_{k}=0$.
If the sequence $\{c_{k}\}$ is not $\ell^{2}$-linearly dependent, then it is said to be  $\ell^{2}$-linearly independent.

nodes.statement:

If $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb {Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ with bound B, then $w_{\varphi}(\xi)\leq B$ a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb {T}^{n}$. Conversely, suppose  $w_{\varphi}(\xi)\leq B$ a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb {T}^{n}$. nodes.name: Condition C (Heisenberg group)
nodes.statement: A function $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ is said to satisfy ``condition C'' if $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda)=0$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1],~\forall~(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\setminus\{(0,0)\}$.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of G_{k,l}^phi
nodes.statement_short: Condition C reduces to $\langle\varphi,L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle=0$ for all $m$ when $(k,l)\neq(0,0)$, via Fourier coefficients of $G_{k,l}^\varphi$.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of G as inner products
nodes.statement:
\widehat{G_{k,l}^{\varphi}}(m)=\int\limits_{0}^{1} G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda) e^{-2\pi im\lambda}d\lambda
=\langle\varphi, L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})}.
nodes.label: 3pr6

nodes.name: Examples satisfying condition C
nodes.statement: We shall first provide some examples of functions in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H})$ which satisfy condition C.

nodes.name: Example 1: product with indicator functions
nodes.statement:
Let $\varphi(x,y,t)=\chi_{[0,2]}(x)\chi_{[0,1]}(y)h(t)$, where $h$ is an arbitrary function in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$. Then
\begin{eqnarray*}
L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi (x,y,t)
&=&\varphi(x-2k,y-l,t-m+\frac{1}{2}(2ky-xl))\\
&=& \chi_{[0,2]}(x-2k)\chi_{[0,1]}(y-l) h(t-m+ky-\frac{l}{2}x)\\
&=& \chi_{[2k,2k+2]}(x)\chi_{[l,l+1]}(y) h(t-m+ky-\frac{l}{2}x).
\end{eqnarray*}
Since for $(k,l)\neq (0,0), [0,2]\times [0,1]~\bigcap~ [2k,2k+2]\times [l,l+1]=\emptyset,$  it follows that $\langle \varphi, L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle=0,~\forall~ m\in\mathbb{Z}$. Then from \eqref{3pr6}, we get $\widehat{G_{k,l}^{\varphi}}(m)=0,~\forall~ m\in\mathbb{Z}$ whenever $(k,l)\neq (0,0)$. Thus $\varphi$ satisfies condition C.
nodes.statement_short: $\chi_{[0,2]}(x)\chi_{[0,1]}(y)h(t)$ satisfies condition C since its lattice translates have disjoint $(x,y)$-supports.

nodes.name: Orthonormality of left translates on the Heisenberg group
nodes.statement: In \cite{ra}, we have proved the theorem that $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is an orthonormal system in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ if and only if $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)=1$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1]$ and $\varphi$ satisfies condition C.
conclusions: $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is an orthonormal system in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ if and only if $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)=1$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1]$ and $\varphi$ satisfies condition C.

nodes.name: Example 2: Gaussian in t
nodes.statement:
We take $h(t)=e^{-t^{2}}, t\in\mathbb{R},$ in Example 1. For this function $h$, the correspond-ing $\varphi$ satisfies $\langle\varphi, L_{(0,0,1)}\varphi\rangle\neq 0$.
Hence $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ does not form an orthonormal system in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H})$.

nodes.name: Example 3: general h
nodes.statement: Instead of $e^{-t^{2}}$, one can take $e^{-|t|}$ or in general any $h\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ for which $\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}}h(t)h(t-1)dt\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Example 4: smooth compactly supported product
nodes.statement_short: Products $f(x)g(y)h(t)$ with $f,g$ having lattice-disjoint supports satisfy condition C; smooth bump examples given.

nodes.name: Example 5: function not satisfying condition C
nodes.statement_short: $\chi_{[0,3]}(x)\chi_{[0,1]}(y)\,\mathrm{sinc}(t)$ fails condition C since $\langle\varphi,L_{(2,0,0)}\varphi\rangle>0$.

nodes.name: Example 6: general products failing condition C
nodes.statement_short: Products $f(x)g(y)h(t)$ with non-vanishing correlation integrals fail condition C.

nodes.name: Canonical dual
nodes.statement: An element $\varphi\in\mathcal{H}$ is said to be a canonical dual to the system $\{f_{k}:k\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ if $\langle f_{k},\varphi\rangle=\delta_{k,0},~\forall~k\in\mathbb{Z}$. In case, if $f_{k}$ is generated from a single function $f$ by some transformation, then $\varphi$ is called a canonical dual to $f$.
nodes.label: 3pdef6

nodes.name: Besselian sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is said to be Besselian if $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{k}f_{k}$ is convergent implies $\{c_{k}\}\in\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$.

nodes.name: Hilbertian sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is said to be Hilbertian if $\{c_{k}\}\in\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$ implies $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{k}f_{k}$ converges.

nodes.name: Saliani's construction of functions with bounded partial sums
